title: Star trails over SEST
caption: Star trails over the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars sweep across the night sky in trails above a retired telescope on a Chilean mountaintop. The instrument is the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope, known as SEST, at ESO's La Silla Observatory in the Atacama Desert.

Star trails like these come from long or stacked exposures. The stars themselves are not racing across the sky; Earth's rotation carries the camera around, so each point of starlight is drawn out into an arc.

SEST was retired in 2003. It was shut down to make way for two newer facilities, the APEX telescope (Atacama Pathfinder Experiment) and the ALMA array (Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array). Even so, the old dish has not been removed. It still stands on its mountain at La Silla, now a quiet foreground for photographs of the turning sky rather than a working instrument.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla Observatory. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points; only a long exposure or a stack of exposures can record their slow motion across the sky as trails.

explore: Submillimetre telescopes collect light at wavelengths longer than infrared but shorter than radio waves, which is useful for studying cold gas and dust. That is why they use dishes rather than the mirrors inside the domes of optical telescopes.
